Full-time employees are eligible for the company benefits in their country from their first day unless a local plan document says otherwise. Contractors receive the equipment and access needed for the engagement, but do not receive employee insurance, retirement, or leave benefits. Questions about your own eligibility should go to People Operations at sara.cohen@novaops.example or through [BambooHR](https://bamboohr.novaops.example). If a local law provides a stronger benefit than this handbook, NovaOps follows the local law. If a signed employment agreement, local plan document, or statutory rule conflicts with this handbook, People Operations confirms which rule controls before payroll or reimbursement is processed. Common edge cases: interns, agency workers, and contractors are not treated as full-time employees unless People Operations issues a NovaOps employment agreement. Part-time employee benefits are handled in the local plan. If you transfer countries, benefits usually move on the effective payroll transfer date. ## Time Off NovaOps provides 20 paid vacation and personal days per calendar year for full-time employees, plus 11 local public holidays based on your work location. We do not use an unlimited PTO policy; we want people to plan real rest and for managers to see when teams are running too hot. Unused vacation rolls over year to year, but your vacation bank is capped at 27 days at any time. Once you reach 27 days, additional accrual pauses until you take time off. Managers should help employees schedule time before they hit the cap. See [state and family leave](stateFMLA.md) for medical, caregiver, and parental leave. Vacation should be requested in BambooHR before you book travel whenever practical. For one or two days, three business days' notice is usually enough; for a week or more, give at least two weeks' notice. A manager may ask you to shift dates for critical coverage, payroll close, incident response, or a launch, but should also offer a realistic alternate window. Holiday calendars follow your regular work location. An employee based in Germany receives the Germany public holiday calendar even during a short visit to the United Kingdom. NovaOps does not usually swap public holidays, but managers may approve a vacation or personal day for observances not on your local list. Q: Do unused vacation days roll over? A: Yes, unused vacation rolls over year to year, but the bank is capped at 27 days and accrual pauses once the cap is reached. After four continuous years at NovaOps, full-time employees may request a one-time 20 working day paid sabbatical. Sabbaticals require manager and People Operations approval, must be planned at least 90 days ahead, and should not be stacked with resignation notice. A request should include dates, coverage notes, and customer or release risks. ## Health, Family, and Retirement NovaOps pays the full employee premium for baseline medical coverage where local plans use premiums, and contributes toward dependent coverage according to the country plan. Dental, vision, mental health support, and statutory social benefits are administered locally. Employees may request a benefits explanation through BambooHR. Baseline medical coverage means the default employee-only plan available in your country. If you choose a richer plan, add dependents, or miss a local enrollment deadline, your payroll deduction may be different. Some countries require local forms before coverage becomes active. For US employees, the 401(k) retirement plan is with Vanguard. You may enroll with your first paycheck. NovaOps matches 100% of your contribution up to 6% of your salary, subject to the plan rules. Employees outside the US receive the retirement or pension contributions required by their local employment plan. Q: Does NovaOps match 401(k) contributions? A: For US employees, yes. The plan is with Vanguard, enrollment may begin with your first paycheck, and NovaOps matches 100% of your contribution up to 6% of salary. Employees outside the United States receive the retirement or pension contributions required by their local employment plan. Primary caregivers welcoming a new child receive up to 16 weeks of leave at 100% pay. Secondary caregivers receive up to 6 weeks at 100% pay. Additional unpaid leave may be available; see [state and family leave](stateFMLA.md). Paid parental leave must be taken within the first year after birth, adoption, surrogacy, or foster placement. Leave may be taken in one block or, with manager and People Operations approval, in two blocks. Q: How much paid parental leave do I get as the primary caregiver? A: Up to 16 weeks at 100% pay. Secondary caregivers receive up to 6 weeks at 100% pay. --- last_updated: 2026-05-06 corpus: handbook audience: all --- # Getting Started ## Before Your First Day Welcome to NovaOps. --- last_updated: 2025-08-29 corpus: handbook audience: all --- # How We Work ## Remote-First, Not Meeting-First NovaOps is hybrid and remote-first. Some employees work near an office, some are fully remote, and all teams must be able to operate without hallway access. The default is written clarity, thoughtful async updates, and meetings only when conversation will improve the decision. Our core collaboration window is 13:00-16:00 UTC on Tuesday through Thursday. Teams may set narrower windows when needed, but managers should protect reasonable working hours in each location. If you are in Israel, Germany, the United Kingdom, or the United States, you are not expected to mirror another region's full day. Local holidays, school pickup windows, and daylight-saving changes create real friction; plan around them. Slack is for short-lived coordination. Jira is for work that needs ownership, priority, or history. GitHub is for code review and engineering decisions. Webex is for live discussion. BambooHR is for HR self-service. Salesforce is for customer and revenue workflows. AWS is used by approved Engineering and IT roles only. For a broader map of systems, see [our internal systems](our-internal-systems.md). ## Async Norms Async work at NovaOps is not silence. It means the next person has enough context to continue without chasing you. A useful async update includes the current state, next step, owner, decision needed, and any deadline that is real rather than merely preferred. If a task is blocked, name the blocker plainly. Prefer posting once with the full situation over sending five tiny messages that force another person to reconstruct your thought process. Use threads for side questions, but summarize the outcome in the main channel or in the Jira issue when the answer changes the work. If a Slack discussion produces a decision, copy the conclusion into Jira, GitHub, or the NovaOps wiki at https://wiki.novaops.example before the thread scrolls away. ## Written Decisions A good NovaOps decision explains the problem, the options considered, the decision, the owner, the date decided, and the review date. Large decisions should be captured in [the NovaOps wiki](https://wiki.novaops.example). Small decisions can live in Jira, GitHub, or Slack if the team can find them later. If a decision affects customers, budget, security, hiring, access, or a release date, write it down. Decision records should be boring and searchable. Use plain titles such as "Decision: delay EU dashboard beta to 2026-09-15" or "Decision: grant temporary Salesforce export access to Customer Success." Include names, dates, system names, ticket IDs, and the chosen alternative. If the decision later changes, add a dated update instead of editing away the original history. GitHub pull requests can serve as engineering decision records when tradeoffs are captured in the description or review comments. For roadmap, staffing, and cross-functional work, use Jira or the NovaOps wiki. For HR topics, do not put private employee details in public team spaces. We do not reward being the fastest person to reply. We reward making work easier for the next person. When you ask for help, include context, the decision you need, the deadline, and what you have already tried. ## Meetings and Live Discussion Meetings are useful when people need to debate, resolve confusion, or make a decision that would sprawl across twenty messages. They are wasteful when the purpose is status reading. Every meeting should have an owner, a purpose, and a desired output. The owner sends context in advance, keeps the group on topic, names decisions as they happen, and posts notes afterward. Calendar titles should be specific: "SupportDesk outage retrospective" is better than "follow-up." If the last two recurring sessions had no decisions, cancel or shorten the series. Default Webex meetings to 25 or 50 minutes. Leave five or ten minutes for people to switch contexts and write notes. If a required decision maker cannot attend, either move the meeting or make the decision async after they can comment. No one is expected to take calls while driving, during medical appointments, on approved leave, or outside reasonable hours just because a calendar invite exists. ## Response Expectations For normal internal messages, a same-business-day response is enough. Managers should set clear goals and review results. Employees should surface risk early, keep commitments visible, and ask for prioritization help when work exceeds capacity. When work crosses departments, name one directly responsible person. A project with five interested leaders and no owner is not owned. A project with one owner and many contributors can move. Accountability is not the same as blame. If a handoff is messy, say what happened and repair the process. If a deadline is slipping, raise it when the risk is visible. Managers should make priorities explicit when work exceeds capacity. ## Disagreement and Conflict Healthy disagreement is part of the job. NovaOps expects people to challenge ideas, not corner people. Say what you see, what risk is being missed, and what decision you recommend. Useful conflict includes Engineering flagging security risk, Customer Success flagging customer impact, Product protecting the current release, or HR saying a manager's timeline does not leave enough room for fair process. Do not use public channels to embarrass someone, relitigate a closed decision, or imply bad intent when a simpler explanation fits. The most useful phrase is often "I disagree because..." followed by a fact, a risk, or a customer impact. If a decision must be made before consensus exists, the accountable owner makes the call, writes down the dissent or tradeoff, and sets a review date.

--- last_updated: 2024-02-21 corpus: handbook audience: all --- # Making a Career ## Growth Philosophy A career at NovaOps is built through increasing judgment, scope, and trust. We do not treat growth as a reward for being busy. We look for evidence that your work is becoming more valuable to customers, teammates, and the company. Every role has a title ladder. The ladder describes the expected level of independence, decision quality, collaboration, and impact. See the title guides for [programmers](titles-for-programmers.md), [designers](titles-for-designers.md), [QA](titles-for-QA.md), [operations](titles-for-ops.md), and [support](titles-for-support.md). The title guides are not scripts; they are shared language for fair conversations. They are also not a point system where enough examples automatically create a new title. Growth can happen through promotion, larger scope, a transfer, people management, or deeper individual contribution at the same title. Sometimes the right next step is not a new title yet. It may be a six-week stretch assignment, clearer decision rights, sharper feedback, or a chance to run a messy cross-functional problem with support. ## Performance Conversations Managers and employees should discuss growth at least quarterly. A useful growth conversation covers what changed in the role, what evidence shows readiness for more scope, what gaps still matter, and what support is needed. Formal written performance reviews happen twice per year, in February and August, and are recorded in BambooHR. Quarterly conversations do not have to wait for the formal review window. If an employee joined recently, changed managers, or transferred teams, the manager should still write down the standard being used, even if the February or August review is short. BambooHR is the source of record for completed written reviews. Supporting examples may live in Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, support cases, design files, customer notes, launch retrospectives, or operating checklists. You should never first hear about a serious performance concern in a formal review. If expectations are unclear, ask your manager to write the expected outcomes, decision rights, and examples of strong work for your level. Managers should name the concern while there is still time to act on it. "Needs more senior judgment" is not enough by itself; the employee should know what decision went wrong, what better judgment would have looked like, and how future work will be evaluated. Good written reviews use examples from the review period and separate impact from style. A messy project that reduced customer risk may be strong evidence even if the plan changed three times. A polished deck with no decision, no shipped improvement, and no clearer customer outcome is weak evidence. If someone is ready for more scope, the review should say what scope. ## Promotion Process NovaOps promotion cycles run twice per year. March proposals take effect April 1, and September proposals take effect October 1. A promotion requires a manager-written packet with evidence from recent work, peer input when relevant, and a mapping to the next title level. Employees may also ask their manager to consider a promotion packet. To be eligible, you generally need at least six months in your current role, sustained performance at your current level, and evidence that you are already operating at the next level in important ways. Tenure alone is not enough. A single intense project is also not enough if the next level requires repeatable judgment. Managers calibrate promotion proposals with People Operations and the department leader. Finance confirms compensation changes before the decision is final. Your manager should not promise a promotion before calibration is complete. ### Promotion Packet Contents A promotion packet should be understandable to a department leader who did not attend every meeting. An HR Operations Specialist normally uses the [operations ladder](titles-for-ops.md), while a QA engineer embedded on a product team normally uses the [QA ladder](titles-for-QA.md). Edge cases should be named directly. If an employee changed managers during the cycle, the old and new manager should agree who owns the packet and which evidence is reliable. If someone transferred teams, the packet should separate evidence from the previous role and evidence in the new role. If the employee has been in title for less than six months, the manager must explain the exception; most short-tenure cases should wait. If a project was canceled, the packet can still use the work if it showed next-level judgment before cancellation. If performance is uneven, calibration may approve a growth plan instead of a promotion. Managers should share the outcome after calibration, not before. A "likely" promotion is still not final until People Operations, the department leader, and Finance have completed their parts. If a packet is declined, the manager should give the employee a written explanation with the specific ladder gaps, the evidence that was missing, and what would make the next cycle stronger. Employees who want consideration should raise it in the quarterly growth conversation before the cycle whenever possible. A missed cycle does not create a backdated promotion by default. --- last_updated: 2024-01-29 corpus: handbook audience: all --- # Severance ## Purpose Severance is meant to give employees a practical landing period when NovaOps ends employment for business reasons or for performance reasons that are not gross misconduct. It is not a substitute for honest performance management, and it is not a promise that every separation will be identical in every country. Local law, employment agreements, and required consultation processes may add rights or process steps. People Operations owns final severance calculations. Managers should not promise a specific package without HR review. This policy is written for retrieval and planning clarity, but it is not a private employment contract. If a local agreement, works council process, statutory notice period, or required consultation process gives a different right, NovaOps follows the more specific rule. People Operations will explain which pieces are company policy and which pieces are local legal process when a separation is being planned. ## Eligibility Employees may be eligible for severance when NovaOps initiates an involuntary separation because of role elimination, restructuring, lack of work, or documented underperformance. Employees are not normally eligible for severance if they resign voluntarily, abandon their job, engage in fraud or serious misconduct, violate confidentiality obligations, or refuse reasonable transition duties during notice. Contractors are governed by their contract and are not covered by this severance policy unless their written agreement says otherwise. Employees on approved family, parental, medical, or disability leave are not excluded from severance eligibility. If a role elimination affects someone on leave, People Operations must review timing, communications, benefits, and local obligations before the manager contacts the employee. Managers should not ask for medical details or pressure someone to return early to discuss a role change. Performance-based severance is available only when the performance process has been documented and People Operations has approved the final separation. A manager who skips coaching, avoids direct feedback, or waits until the last day of a project should not assume severance can clean up a poor process. See the manager playbook for the underperformance process; the employee-facing fact is simpler: NovaOps expects serious concerns to be communicated before they become separation decisions, except in cases of misconduct or severe risk. ## Formula The base severance amount is 4 weeks of regular base pay. Once an employee has at least one completed year of NovaOps service, NovaOps adds 2 weeks of regular base pay for each completed year of service. Severance is capped at 16 weeks of pay, which is treated as 4 months for policy purposes. Examples: an employee with less than one completed year receives 4 weeks. An employee with 2 completed years receives 8 weeks: 4 base weeks plus 2 weeks for each completed year. An employee with 3 completed years receives 10 weeks. An employee with 8 completed years would calculate to 20 weeks, but the cap limits the severance payment to 16 weeks. The formula uses completed years of continuous NovaOps service, measured from the employee's most recent full-time employee start date through the last paid day. Partial years do not round up. If an employee was a contractor and later became an employee, contractor time does not count unless the written conversion agreement says it does. If an employee transferred countries, People Operations will review whether the local employment record treats the service as continuous. Regular base pay means normal salary or base wages before bonuses, commissions, referral awards, spot recognition, equity, expense reimbursements, or allowances. For Sales employees, severance is not calculated from pipeline value or expected commissions. For employees with a recent approved compensation change, Finance and People Operations decide whether the new rate or prior rate applies based on the effective date. Common examples: an employee with 1 completed year receives 6 weeks: 4 base weeks plus 2 weeks for one completed year. An employee with 4 completed years receives 12 weeks. An employee with 6 completed years receives 16 weeks because the formula would reach the cap. Good design here is not decoration after requirements are finished. It is product judgment, systems thinking, customer empathy, and the ability to make complex operations feel understandable. Design titles measure scope and influence. A designer can grow by becoming a stronger individual contributor, by leading larger product areas, or eventually by managing people. Management is not required for senior design impact. Design sits in Product and works daily with Product Management, Engineering, QA, Customer Success, Support, Sales, and Operations. The same ladder applies to product design, interaction design, UX design, design systems work, and research-heavy product design. Some designers may spend most of a cycle on customer workflow mapping, while others spend more time on Figma components, Jira acceptance criteria, or launch validation. --- last_updated: 2026-02-01 corpus: handbook audience: all --- # Titles for Ops ## What Ops Means Here Operations at NovaOps includes the people who make the company run: HR, IT, Finance, Sales Operations, Customer Success Operations, and cross-functional program work. Ops work is often quiet until it fails, so our titles are designed to recognize prevention, clarity, judgment, and repeatable systems. Ops titles are used across departments with local examples. A Sales Operations Specialist may spend more time in Salesforce; an IT Operations Specialist may spend more time in Okta, Slack, or the laptop fleet; an HR Operations Specialist may spend more time in BambooHR. A Finance Operations Specialist may spend more time in billing review, approvals, reimbursement queues, or vendor renewal tracking. A Customer Success Operations employee may spend more time in Salesforce, SupportDesk, Webex seat routing, renewal health views, and customer handoff data. A Program Operations employee may spend more time in Jira, Webex, written decision records, launch calendars, and cross-functional dependency tracking. The level expectations are the same even when the tools differ. The ops ladder is not a prize for having the most urgent Slack mentions. It is a way to name the scope and reliability of operational judgment. Strong operations work makes the right action easier for everyone else. It catches a missing approval before payroll is blocked, rejects an overbroad GitHub request before source code exposure, clarifies a stale manager record before access goes to the wrong approver, or turns a recurring Salesforce cleanup issue into a durable field rule and enablement note. Ops employees usually work in systems that contain sensitive records. Okta controls login and MFA. BambooHR contains employee records and HR self-service. Salesforce contains customer and revenue information. Webex and Slack support collaboration. GitHub contains source code. Jira tracks planned work and cross-team delivery. AWS contains production and internal cloud resources. Billing and vendor review systems contain cost, contract, and renewal data. The more senior the ops work, the more important it is to understand not only the tool, but the business decision, data sensitivity, approval path, and handoff risk behind the tool. Operations at NovaOps is remote-first work. A clean process should work across Israel, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States without requiring hallway knowledge or one person's memory. Good ops work has an owner, a written trail, a clear approval path, a review date when needed, and a backup path when the normal owner is on leave. ## How Ops Titles Are Used The O1 through O5 ladder applies to operations work even when the local job title uses different words. HR Coordinator, HR Generalist, People Operations Lead, IT Support Specialist, Systems Administrator, Finance Controller, Sales Operations Specialist, Customer Success Operations Specialist, Program Operations Lead, and Operations Manager may all use this ladder when the work being evaluated is operational work. The ladder level comes from scope, judgment, independence, and durable impact, not from the noun in the job title. Some roles sit partly on another ladder. A Customer Success Manager whose main work is customer relationship ownership should use the support and customer success ladder. A software engineer building internal tools should usually use the programmer ladder. A Product Manager running a launch calendar may use program operations examples for a stretch assignment, but that does not automatically move the person onto the ops ladder. When the ladder choice is debatable, the manager should explain which work is being evaluated and why. See [making a career](making-a-career.md) for promotion packet expectations. Ops titles also do not grant access by themselves. Okta admin, BambooHR administrator, Salesforce admin, GitHub organization admin, AWS admin, Jira project admin, Webex admin, billing review, and export rights are granted by business need and approval. An O1 builds trust by being reliable with sensitive details. The team helps customers use workflow automation safely and effectively, turns recurring pain into product feedback, and protects trust during incidents. Support titles recognize customer judgment, product fluency, written clarity, and the ability to solve problems without creating new ones. Support work includes reactive support cases, proactive customer health work, onboarding help, renewal-risk discovery, incident communication, and the translation of customer pain into useful Product and Engineering signal. Some employees carry "Support" titles and spend most of the day in SupportDesk. Others carry "Customer Success" titles and split time among Salesforce account work, Webex customer conversations, SupportDesk follow-up, and internal coordination. The ladder below applies when the work is primarily customer-facing problem solving inside Customer Success. Support employees usually work in Salesforce, Slack, Webex, Jira, SupportDesk, and approved customer communication channels. Access is granted by role and reviewed when someone changes teams. Salesforce is used for account context, contacts, renewal risk, contract-sensitive notes, and customer health. SupportDesk is used for support cases, customer-visible updates, internal notes, tags, severity, and handoff history. Jira is used when a customer issue needs Product, Engineering, QA, or release work. Webex is used for live customer calls when written support will not resolve confusion quickly enough or when trust needs a human conversation. Slack is for internal coordination, but durable decisions should be copied into Salesforce, SupportDesk, Jira, or the NovaOps wiki according to the subject. Support employees should understand the difference between helping, promising, and committing the company. A support employee may explain documented behavior, collect evidence, route a case, propose a workaround, and set a next update time. A support employee should not promise a release date, offer contractual concessions, approve billing changes, disclose security details beyond approved language, or guarantee a root cause before Engineering has confirmed it. When in doubt, preserve trust by saying what is known, what is being checked, who owns the next step, and when the customer will hear back. ## Tools and Records Support quality depends on leaving a record that the next person can trust. A customer should not have to repeat the same story because the previous support note was vague, and an engineer should not have to reconstruct a defect from a chat summary. Use SupportDesk for the customer-facing ticket, severity, timestamps, troubleshooting evidence, internal notes, attachments that are approved for support handling, and the final resolution. Promotion evidence should separate activity from impact. "Handled 400 tickets" is incomplete. "Reduced repeat onboarding tickets by changing the admin setup guide, creating a SupportDesk macro, and opening a Jira request for confusing copy" is stronger. "Joined many customer calls" is incomplete. "Led three at-risk customer recovery plans, kept Salesforce risk current, and prevented unsupported roadmap commitments while restoring executive trust" is stronger. Managers should include the hard parts. A promotion packet is more credible when it names the ambiguity, risk, or tradeoff. If Rachel Stein resolved a Webex-related customer follow-up problem, the packet should explain how she protected the customer experience despite the tool constraint. If Maya Cohen owned a troubled onboarding account, the packet should describe what decisions she made, what help she asked for, and what changed for the customer. If Yael Romano sponsors an S4 promotion, the evidence should show that the employee improved support quality beyond their personal relationships with customers. ## What Does Not Count Some work is useful but not promotion evidence by itself. This section is not meant to dismiss effort. It helps managers and employees avoid confusing motion with level. Weak or incomplete evidence includes: - Closing many simple cases without improving customer outcomes or support quality. - Being friendly in Webex calls while someone else owns the hard decisions. - Staying online late as a habit instead of improving escalation paths or coverage. - Escalating everything to Engineering to look urgent. - Avoiding escalation until the customer loses trust. - Writing long internal updates that do not name the decision, owner, evidence, or next step. - Receiving Slack praise that is not tied to customer impact or level expectations. - Owning a crisis that the employee helped create through poor handoff, overpromising, or missing evidence. - Becoming the only person who knows how to handle a case type instead of documenting and teaching it. - Pushing for a customer exception that violates access, billing, security, or contract boundaries. - Creating duplicate Salesforce, SupportDesk, and Jira records that disagree with each other. A customer saying "thank you" is good, but it does not automatically prove seniority. A customer being angry does not automatically prove the support employee did anything wrong.
